- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% of recent mean or median.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–3% of recent mean or median.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 5 days, model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% per day of lag.
- Mean reversion patterns (forecast > true by >10% for 3+ consecutive days) should trigger downward correction, especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in first 5 days, model is likely underestimating momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating ±1.0), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before adjustment.
